title: Protests in Kolkata, the Holwell Monument Movement, and CID Surveillance

questions.question: In which city did Subhas Chandra Bose organize mass protests against British rule?

options.A: Kolkata
options.D: Tokyo

questions.answer_text: Bose organized mass protests in Kolkata against colonial decisions.

questions.question: What colonial monument did Netaji want removed from Dalhousie Square?

options.A: Holwell Monument
options.D: Statue of Liberty

questions.answer_text: Netaji called for the removal of the Holwell monument in Kolkata.

questions.question: Where did the Holwell monument stand in Kolkata?

options.A: Dalhousie Square
options.D: Victoria Memorial

questions.answer_text: The Holwell monument stood at the corner of Dalhousie Square.

questions.question: What did the British authorities do to Subhas after the protests?

options.A: Threw him into jail
options.D: Sent him on vacation

questions.answer_text: British authorities arrested Subhas and threw him into jail.

questions.question: How did Netaji protest inside the British jail?

options.A: By going on a hunger strike
options.D: By singing songs

questions.answer_text: Netaji went on a courageous hunger strike in jail.

questions.question: How many days did Netaji's hunger strike in jail last?

options.A: 7 days
options.D: 30 days

questions.answer_text: Netaji was released following a 7-day hunger strike.

questions.question: Where was Netaji kept after his release from jail?

options.A: Under house arrest in his Kolkata house
options.D: In a school

questions.answer_text: Netaji was kept under house arrest at his residence in Kolkata.

questions.question: Which police agency kept Netaji's house under strict watch?

options.A: British CID
options.D: Forest Rangers

questions.answer_text: The British CID kept his Kolkata house under constant surveillance.

questions.question: Was Netaji afraid of the British police watching his house?

options.A: No, he remained brave and determined
options.D: He decided to help the British

questions.answer_text: Netaji was fearless and never gave up on freeing India.

questions.question: What does a hunger strike mean?

options.A: Refusing to eat food as a peaceful protest
options.D: Buying snacks

questions.answer_text: A hunger strike means refusing to eat food as a powerful form of moral protest.

questions.question: Why did Subhas Chandra Bose organize mass protests in Kolkata?
questions.reference_answer: Subhas Chandra Bose organized mass protests in Kolkata because the British declared war on India's behalf without consulting Indian leaders, and to remove the Holwell monument.

questions.question: What happened to Netaji when he was arrested and put into jail?
questions.reference_answer: Netaji went on a 7-day hunger strike in jail, which forced the British authorities to release him and place him under house arrest.

questions.question: Say the name of the monument Netaji protested against:
questions.reference_answer: Holwell Monument

questions.question: Say the method of protest Netaji used inside jail:
questions.reference_answer: Hunger Strike

questions.question: Say the name of the square in Kolkata where the monument stood:
questions.reference_answer: Dalhousie Square

questions.question: Why did the Holwell monument cause intense public outrage among Indian nationalists?

options.A: It commemorated a biased colonial narrative of the Black Hole of Calcutta insulting Indian history
options.B: It blocked the roadway for street cars
options.C: It was built from low quality bricks
options.D: It had incorrect English spellings on its plaque

questions.answer_text: The Holwell Monument symbolized colonial falsehoods and British imperial arrogance in Bengal.

questions.question: What political tactic did the British colonial government adopt after releasing Bose from jail?

options.A: Confinement under strict CID surveillance at his Elgin Road house
options.B: Deporting him to the Andaman Cellular Jail
options.D: Giving him a passport to travel abroad freely

questions.answer_text: The British placed Bose under strict house arrest with round-the-clock CID surveillance.

questions.question: Why did the British government release Subhas from jail during his 7-day hunger strike?

options.A: They feared mass uprisings and riots across India if Netaji died in colonial custody
options.B: They ran out of prison food
options.C: The British judges apologized to him
options.D: His prison term expired naturally

questions.answer_text: The British feared uncontrollable public fury if Bose died in custody.

questions.question: What was the purpose of British CID surveillance around Netaji's residence?

options.A: To prevent him from communicating with revolutionaries and escaping the country
options.B: To guard his family from thieves
options.C: To deliver daily newspapers to his porch
options.D: To record radio programs with him

questions.answer_text: CID surveillance aimed to isolate Netaji and block his contact with freedom fighters.

questions.question: Which prominent location in Kolkata was Dalhousie Square, where the movement took place?

options.A: The administrative heart and power center of the British Raj in Kolkata (BBD Bagh)
options.D: The botanical gardens across the river

questions.answer_text: Dalhousie Square was the political and commercial headquarters of British colonial authority.

questions.question: How did Netaji's agitation for removing the Holwell Monument unite diverse communities?

options.A: It brought together Hindus and Muslims in common solidarity against colonial insults
options.C: It was supported by the British army officers
options.D: It focused solely on businessmen

questions.answer_text: The Holwell movement forged strong Hindu-Muslim unity against imperialist symbols.

questions.question: What did Netaji's willingness to undertake a hunger strike demonstrate about his resolve?

options.A: Supreme moral courage and readiness to sacrifice his life for Indian dignity
options.D: A test of hospital staff

questions.answer_text: His hunger strike proved his unwavering commitment to put national dignity above life itself.

questions.question: In what year did the British declare India a belligerent in World War II without Indian consent?
questions.answer_text: In September 1939, Britain dragged India into WWII without consulting Indian representatives.

questions.question: Explain the significance of the Holwell Monument movement launched by Netaji in Kolkata.
questions.reference_answer: Netaji launched the Holwell Monument movement to remove a colonial symbol of humiliation at Dalhousie Square. It demonstrated anti-imperialist resistance and united Hindus and Muslims in common protest.

questions.question: Describe how Netaji's hunger strike in jail forced the British government to change their tactics.
questions.reference_answer: When Netaji was jailed, he began a fast unto death. The British feared massive civil unrest and violence if he died in prison, so they released him to house arrest under tight CID surveillance.

questions.question: Why did the British CID place Netaji's residence under round-the-clock surveillance?
questions.reference_answer: The CID kept Netaji under continuous surveillance to monitor his movements, cut off his communication with revolutionary groups, and prevent him from escaping or mobilizing mass revolts.

questions.question: Pronounce the police intelligence wing that monitored Netaji:
questions.reference_answer: British CID Surveillance

questions.question: Pronounce the duration of Netaji's historic prison protest:
questions.reference_answer: Seven Day Hunger Strike

questions.question: Pronounce the historic Kolkata protest location:
questions.reference_answer: Dalhousie Square Kolkata

questions.question: Pronounce the condition Netaji was placed under at his residence:
questions.reference_answer: Strict House Arrest

questions.question: What strategic imperative compelled Netaji to challenge the Holwell monument in July 1940?

options.A: To synthesize anti-imperial sentiment and dismantle colonial psychological subjugation while Britain was weakened by World War II
options.B: To facilitate commercial real estate development in central Calcutta
options.C: To comply with municipal architectural renovation regulations
options.D: To resolve a private legal dispute between local landlords

questions.answer_text: Netaji utilized the Holwell movement as a catalyst for a broader anti-colonial offensive during Britain's wartime vulnerability.

questions.question: Under which draconian emergency legislation was Subhas Chandra Bose detained in July 1940?

options.A: Defense of India Rules
options.D: Indian Arms Act

questions.answer_text: Bose was arrested under the wartime Defense of India Rules to preempt his planned mass demonstration on July 3, 1940.

questions.question: What profound philosophical statement did Netaji write to the Governor of Bengal during his hunger strike?

options.A: One individual may die for an idea, but that idea will, after his death, incarnate itself in a thousand lives
options.B: All warfare is based on deception and patience
options.C: A compromise is always better than persistent struggle
options.D: Colonial rule can be reformed through gradual constitutional petitions

questions.answer_text: Netaji's famous prison letter proclaimed that one's sacrifice would reincarnate into the spirit of thousands fighting for freedom.

questions.question: How did Netaji utilize his house arrest at Elgin Road between December 1940 and January 1941?

options.A: He feigned complete spiritual seclusion and silence while secretly orchestrating the logistics of his clandestine international escape
options.B: He retired permanently from national politics
options.C: He drafted legal briefs for the High Court of Calcutta
options.D: He accepted an advisory post with the colonial administration

questions.answer_text: Netaji adopted a posture of religious seclusion, growing a beard and misleading British spies while planning the Great Escape.

questions.question: Why did the British authorities eventually dismantle the Holwell Monument after Netaji's arrest?

options.A: To appease the intensifying nationwide agitation and prevent a total breakdown of law and order in the colonial capital
options.B: Because it was damaged by lightning
options.C: At the formal request of the King of England
options.D: To replace it with a clock tower

questions.answer_text: Even with Bose behind bars, the momentum of his movement forced Governor Sir John Herbert to remove the monument.

questions.question: What psychological dilemma confronted the British Raj regarding Subhas Bose's hunger strike?

options.A: Martyrdom in prison would spark uncontrollable revolution, whereas releasing him posed an enormous security risk to imperial wartime operations
options.B: They could not find a medical doctor to examine him
options.C: They were worried about international trade sanctions from neutral countries
options.D: They lacked the legal authority to maintain prison facilities

questions.answer_text: The British were caught in a double bind: his death in custody would ignite mass revolt, but his release enabled anti-colonial leadership.

questions.question: How did Netaji's actions during this crisis embody the forward-bloc revolutionary doctrine?

options.A: By proactively seizing the geopolitical window of Britain's war entanglement to demand immediate, unconditional independence
options.B: By advocating passive neutrality and waiting for peace negotiations
options.C: By lobbying British political parties for constitutional concessions
options.D: By proposing partition of the subcontinent

questions.answer_text: Bose's Forward Bloc ideology demanded exploiting Britain's wartime vulnerability ('Britain's difficulty is India's opportunity').

questions.question: Critically analyze why Netaji regarded Britain's unilateral entry of India into World War II as an intolerable assault on Indian sovereignty.
questions.reference_answer: Netaji asserted that dragging 400 million Indians into a destructive imperialist war without the consent of their representatives was the ultimate denial of sovereignty, requiring uncompromising mass resistance rather than cooperative compromise.

questions.question: Examine the moral and political rationale behind Netaji's decision to stage a fast unto death in Presidency Jail.
questions.reference_answer: Netaji recognized that colonial incarceration was designed to immobilize him during a critical global crisis. His hunger strike was a calculated moral weapon demonstrating that life without freedom was worthless, placing moral culpability directly upon the British administration.

questions.question: Explain the strategic significance of the British CID surveillance network and how Netaji outmaneuvered it.
questions.reference_answer: The British deployed a dense network of CID agents around 38/2 Elgin Road. Netaji outmaneuvered them through psychological deception, adopting spiritual isolation, growing a beard, and preparing a clandestine motor escape right under their watch.

questions.question: Synthesize how the events of 1940 (Holwell agitation, imprisonment, hunger strike, house arrest) served as the prelude to Netaji's international crusade.
questions.reference_answer: These events convinced Netaji that constitutional protests and domestic civil disobedience inside India were insufficient to dislodge the British Empire. This realization directly compelled him to seek international military alliances abroad to liberate India by force of arms.

sequence_test.title: Chronological Sequence of the Holwell Movement, Imprisonment, and House Arrest
sequence_test.description: Evaluate the timeline of events from the mass protests in Kolkata to Netaji's confinement under CID surveillance.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of events following the outbreak of WWII and Netaji's protests in Kolkata?

options.A: Mass protests for Holwell Monument removal -> Arrest under Defense of India Rules -> 7-Day Hunger Strike in prison -> Release to house arrest under CID surveillance
options.B: House arrest -> Holwell Monument protests -> 7-Day Hunger Strike -> Arrest
options.C: 7-Day Hunger Strike -> House arrest -> Holwell protests -> Prison arrest
options.D: CID surveillance -> 7-Day Hunger Strike -> Holwell protests -> Release

questions.answer_text: The sequence started with mass protests at Dalhousie Square, his subsequent arrest, his heroic 7-day hunger strike, and release into strict house arrest.

questions.question: Arrange the strategic milestones of Netaji's resistance during 1940 in chronological order:

options.A: Demanding removal of colonial monuments -> Incarceration by colonial administration -> Fast unto death moral protest -> Tactical feigning of seclusion at Elgin Road
options.B: Seclusion at Elgin Road -> Incarceration -> Monument removal -> Fast unto death
options.C: Fast unto death -> Seclusion -> Monument removal -> Incarceration
options.D: Incarceration -> Seclusion -> Monument removal -> Fast unto death

questions.answer_text: Netaji led the monument agitation, endured prison, won his release through a fast unto death, and established seclusion at Elgin Road.
